arxiv-1712-08349.title: Tracking the Diffusion of Named Entities Conference: ; December 2017;
arxiv-1712-08349.creator: Matthew Rowe, Leon Derczynski
arxiv-1712-08349.description: Abstract . Existing studies of how information diffuses across social networks have thus far concentrated on analysing and recovering the spread of deterministic innovations such as URLs, hashtags, and group membership. However investigating how mentions of real-world entities appear and spread has yet to be explored, largely due to the computationally intractable nature of performing large-scale entity extraction.

arxiv-1912-05007.title: Oktoberfest Food Dataset
arxiv-1912-05007.creator: Alexander Ziller, Julius Hansjakob, Vitalii Rusinov, Daniel Zügner, Peter Vogel, Stephan Günnemann
arxiv-1912-05007.description: Abstract We release a realistic, diverse, and challenging dataset for object detection on images. The data was recorded at a beer tent in Germany and consists of 15 different categories of food and drink items. We created more than 2,500 object annotations by hand for 1,110 images captured by a video camera above the checkout.

arxiv-2105-05433.title: Stability of Syzygy bundles corresponding to stable vector bundles on algebraic surfaces
arxiv-2105-05433.creator: SURATNO BASU, SARBESWAR PAL
arxiv-2105-05433.description: Abstract . Let ( X , H ) (X,H) be a polarized smooth projective algebraic surface and E E is globally generated, stable vector bundle on X X . Then the Syzygy bundle M E M_{E} associated to it is defined as the kernel bundle corresponding to the evaluation map.

arxiv-2109-12617.title: Structure-aware scale-adaptive networks for cancer segmentation in whole-slide images
arxiv-2109-12617.creator: Yibao Sun, Giussepi Lopez, Yaqi Wang, Xingru Huang, Huiyu Zhou, Qianni Zhang
arxiv-2109-12617.description: Abstract Cancer segmentation in whole-slide images is a fundamental step for viable tumour burden estimation, which is of great value for cancer assessment. However, factors like vague boundaries or small regions dissociated from viable tumour areas make it a challenging task.

arxiv-2205-00873.title: A generalization of Newton-Maclaurin’s inequalities Thanks: Research of author is supported by an NSFC Grant No. 11871243
arxiv-2205-00873.creator: Changyu Ren
arxiv-2205-00873.description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Changyu Ren. In this paper, we prove Newton-Maclaurin type inequalities for functions obtained by linear combination of two neighboring primary symmetry functions, which is a generalization of the classical Newton-Maclaurin inequality. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification
26D05, 26D15

1. Introduction

The
k
-th elementary symmetric function of the variables

x_{1},x_{2},\cdots,x_{n}
is defined by

\sigma_{k}(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{1\leq i_{1}<\cdots<i_{k}\leq n}x_{i_{1}}\cdots x_{i_{k}},\quad 1\leq k\leq n,

where
x=(x_{1},x_{2},\cdots,x_{n})
. For example, when
n=3
,

\displaystyle\sigma_{1}(x)=x_{1}+x_{2}+x_{3},\quad\sigma_{2}(x)=x_{1}x_{2}+x_{1}x_{3}+x_{2}x_{3},\quad\sigma_{n}(x)=x_{1}x_{2}x_{3}. It will be convenient to define
\sigma_{0}(x)=1
, and define

\sigma_{k}(x)=0
if
k<0
or
k>n
.

arxiv-2208-07293.title: First Search for Axion-Like Particles in a Storage Ring Using a Polarized Deuteron Beam
arxiv-2208-07293.creator: S. Karanth, E.J. Stephenson, S.P. Chang, V. Hejny, J. Pretz, Y.K. Semertzidis, A. Wirzba, A. Wrońska, F. Abusaif, A. Aksentev, B. Alberdi, A. Aggarwal, A. Andres, L. Barion, I. Bekman, M. Beyß, C. Böhme, B. Breitkreutz, C. von Byern, N. Canale, G. Ciullo, S. Dymov, N.-O. Fröhlich, R. Gebel, K. Grigo
arxiv-2208-07293.description: Abstract Based on the notion that the local dark-matter field of axions or axion-like particles (ALPs) in our Galaxy induces oscillating couplings to the spins of nucleons and nuclei (via the electric dipole moment of the latter and/or the paramagnetic axion-wind effect), we establish the feasibility of a new method to search for ALPs in storage rings.

arxiv-2408-06674.title: Compact robotic gripper with tandem actuation for selective fruit harvesting
arxiv-2408-06674.creator: Alejandro Velasquez, Cindy Grimm, Joseph R. Davidson
arxiv-2408-06674.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Alejandro Velasquez, Cindy Grimm, Joseph R. Davidson. Selective fruit harvesting is a challenging manipulation problem due to occlusions and clutter arising from plant foliage. A harvesting gripper should i) have a small cross-section, to avoid collisions while approaching the fruit; ii) have a soft and compliant grasp to adapt to different fruit geometry and avoid bruising it; and iii) be capable of rigidly holding the fruit tightly enough to counteract detachment forces.

arxiv-2409-00394.title: The behaviour of a certain additive function in large intervals between consecutive primes
arxiv-2409-00394.creator: Michael Th. Rassias
arxiv-2409-00394.description: Abstract . We investigate the behaviour of a certain additive function depending on prime divisors of specific integers lying in large gaps between consecutive primes. The result is obtained by a combination of results and ideas related to large gaps between primes and the Erdös-Kac theorem, especially the Kubilius model from Probabilistic Number Theory.

arxiv-2510-02834.title: Hunt for the mHz variability in the TESS and XMM-Newton observations of nova-like cataclysmic variables Facilities: TESS, XMM-Newton astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 ) , GNUPLOT ( http://www.gnuplot.info/ ), SAS ( htt
arxiv-2510-02834.creator: Andrej Dobrotka, Jozef Magdolen, Martin Melicherčík
arxiv-2510-02834.description: Abstract We analysed the flickering of selected nova-like cataclysmic variables observed by the TESS satellite and XMM-Newton . We searched for break frequencies ( f b f_{\rm b} ) in the corresponding power density spectra (PDS), and for any long-term evolution.

pmc-11345716.title: Reconfigurable Optical Sensor for Metal-Ion-Mediated Label-Free Recognition of Different Biomolecular Targets
pmc-11345716.creator: Tiziano Di Giulio, Martina Corsi, Francesco Gagliani, Giuseppe De Benedetto, Cosimino Malitesta, Aurora Mazzei, Amilcare Barca, Tiziano Verri, Giuseppe Barillaro, Elisabetta Mazzotta
pmc-11345716.description: Reconfiguration of chemical sensors, intended as the capacity of the sensor to adapt to novel operational scenarios, e.g., new target analytes, is potentially game changing and would enable rapid and cost-effective reaction to dynamic changes occurring at healthcare, environmental, and industrial levels. Yet, it is still a challenge, and rare examples of sensor reconfiguration have been reported to date.

pmc-12420153.title: Shifting Perspectives: The Importance of Assessing Suicide Risk in Medically Ill Patients Without Psychiatric History
pmc-12420153.creator: V. H. Santos, F. M. Tehrani, M. Pires, R. P. Andrade, B. Sousa, Z. C. e Sá, T. Carvalhão, S. Fontes
pmc-12420153.description: IntroductionChronic medical conditions are increasingly recognized as significant contributors to suicide risk, especially in patients without prior psychiatric diagnoses (Østergaard et al. JAMA Psychiatry 2024). This case examines the psychiatric impact in a 65-year-old male admitted to general surgery for abdominal pain, who subsequently underwent an ileocolectomy for suspected gastrointestinal malignancy.

pmc-12560118.title: T‐cell subsets in Pneumocystis pneumonia
pmc-12560118.creator: Yuxi Chen, Hengmo Rong, Ting Li, Chao Zhang, Huqin Yang, Han Sun, Dong Wang, Xiaoxia Zhou, Kan Zhai, Zhaohui Tong
pmc-12560118.description: Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP), caused by the opportunistic fungal pathogen Pneumocystis, remains a common fungal infection among immunosuppressed individuals. T cells are known to play a critical role in host defences against Pneumocystis. Two functional groups of T cells exist: CD4+ T and CD8+ T.

pmc-12722994.title: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor is associated with monocytic AML and innate immune resistance reversible with an AHR inhibitor
pmc-12722994.creator: Jennifer N. Saultz, Daniel Bottomly, Faith Burns, Kaelan Byrd, Yoko Kosaka, Bernhard Alber, Daniel Chandra, Stephen E. Kurtz, Guang Fan, Andy Kaempf, Nicola Long, Marta Sanchez-Martin, Lei Wang, Karen McGovern, Dan S. Kaufman, Shannon K. McWeeney, Brian J. Druker, Jeffrey W. Tyner, Evan F. Lind
pmc-12722994.description: BackgroundAcute myeloid leukemia (AML) is characterized by a complex interplay between genomic alterations, aberrant hematopoiesis, and immune evasion. The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) pathway is a critical player in this phenomenon determining the fate of stem cell differentiation as well as dictating immune cell development and function.

pmc-12731644.title: Familial Risk Factors in Thyroid Cancer Across Generations and Geographics: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12731644.creator: Madeleine B. Landau, Natalie J. Mikhailov, Amreena Singh, Ebtihag O. Alenzi, Baraah Abu Alsel, Mohammed M. Ismail, Manal S. Fawzy, Eman A. Toraih
pmc-12731644.description: Simple SummaryThyroid cancer rates are increasing worldwide, and having family members with thyroid cancer may raise a person’s risk of developing the disease. While it is known that family history is important, we did not know exactly how much risk was linked to different types of family relationships or whether it varied by country.

pmc-13116086.title: Bridging the Care Gap: Family Support for Adults Living with Diabetes Mellitus in Limpopo Province, South Africa
pmc-13116086.creator: Selina Motsharine-Ndou, Lina Sebolaisi Hlahla, Dorah Ursula Ramathuba
pmc-13116086.description: Highlights Public health relevance—How does this work relate to a public health issue? Diabetes mellitus is a major public burden in South Africa, specifically in the rural communities where there are resource limitations.The study highlights that family support is critical, but not fully utilized, in diabetes mellitus self-management support. Public health significance—Why is this work of significance to public health?

pmc-13450779.title: Impact assessment of effective rounds of mass drug administration against schistosomiasis and soil transmitted helminthiasis among school age children in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria
pmc-13450779.creator: Kenneth Nnamdi Opara, Clement Ameh Yaro, Nnamso Williams Ikpeida, Aliyu Mohammed, Hadiza Joy Marcus, Kingsley Azu, Salisu Ahmad, Esther Sunday Okon, Ellie Leaning, Moses Aderogba, Louise-Makau Barasa, Antia Etop, Ime Sylvester Udoh, Fatai Oyediran, Imabong O. Umah, Solomon M. Jacob, Gideon U. Ntuen,
pmc-13450779.description: BackgroundSchistosomiasis (SCH) and Soil-transmitted helminthiasis (STH) remain major neglected tropical diseases across sub-Saharan Africa. In Akwa Ibom State, preventive chemotherapy (PC) has been implemented in endemic Local Government Areas (LGAs). This study assessed the impact of five effective rounds of PC on the prevalence and intensity of SCH and STH in 26 endemic LGAs.
